subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Pelvic inflammatory disease, Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome and vaginitis differential

steps.tx: Ascending infection of the upper female genital tract defines **pelvic inflammatory disease**. The clinical spectrum encompasses endometritis, salpingitis, tubo-ovarian abscess, and pelvic peritonitis. While sexually transmitted pathogens Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Mycoplasma genitalium initiate the breach of cervical defenses, subsequent tubal tissue destruction is mediated by mixed aerobic and anaerobic vaginal bacteria.
steps.say: Pelvic inflammatory disease is an ascending infection affecting the uterus, fallopian tubes, and pelvic peritoneum. Chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and mycoplasma initiate the infection, which is then exacerbated by mixed aerobic and anaerobic vaginal flora.

steps.tx: Due to the severe reproductive consequences of delayed intervention, the threshold for treating PID is deliberately kept low. Presumptive diagnosis requires pelvic pain plus one or more **clinical triad criteria**: cervical motion tenderness (the chandelier sign), uterine tenderness, or adnexal tenderness on bimanual pelvic examination in a sexually active woman. Additional supportive signs include purulent cervical discharge, fever, and elevated inflammatory markers.
steps.say: Because untreated infection damages fertility, treatment begins promptly. Diagnosis requires lower pelvic pain plus cervical motion tenderness, uterine tenderness, or adnexal tenderness on examination. Fever and purulent discharge provide supportive confirmation.

steps.tx: Lower genital tract infections presenting with abnormal vaginal discharge mandate precise differentiation of the **vaginitis triad**. Bacterial vaginosis reflects loss of protective hydrogen peroxide-producing Lactobacillus acidophilus with overgrowth of Gardnerella vaginalis and anaerobes. Trichomonas vaginalis produces a flagellated protozoal sexually transmitted infection, whereas Candida albicans represents opportunistic fungal pseudo-hyphal proliferation triggered by antibiotics, pregnancy, or uncontrolled diabetes.
steps.say: Vaginal discharge requires distinguishing between three common infections. Bacterial vaginosis involves lactobacilli loss with anaerobic overgrowth. Trichomoniasis is a parasitic sexually transmitted infection, while candida represents opportunistic yeast proliferation.

steps.tx: In patients with PID who develop localized pleuritic right upper quadrant pain, **Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome** must be recognized. This complication arises from transperitoneal or lymphatic spread of Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae to the anterior liver capsule, causing fibrinous perihepatitis without deep parenchymal hepatic involvement. Diagnostic laparoscopy classically reveals delicate violin-string fibrinous adhesions bridging the anterior hepatic surface to the abdominal wall.
steps.say: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome occurs when chlamydia or gonorrhoea spreads to the liver capsule, causing right upper quadrant pain. Laparoscopy classically reveals delicate violin-string adhesions bridging between the liver and abdominal wall.
